summary: Dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) is an oral, extended-release potassium channel blocker indicated to improve walking in adults with multiple sclerosis, demonstrated by an increase in walking speed. The dose is fixed at 10 mg twice daily approximately 12 hours apart; higher doses provide no added benefit and substantially increase the risk of seizures. Because the drug is eliminated almost entirely by the kidneys, it accumulates in renal impairment and is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment (CrCl <=50 mL/min) and in patients with a history of seizures. Other key risks are anaphylaxis and urinary tract infections.
indications: To improve walking in adults with multiple sclerosis (demonstrated by an increase in walking speed)

moa: Dalfampridine is a broad-spectrum potassium channel blocker. By blocking voltage-gated potassium channels on the surface of demyelinated axons, it prolongs the action potential and improves conduction of nerve impulses along damaged nerve fibers. The exact mechanism by which this translates into improved walking in multiple sclerosis is not fully established, but enhanced axonal conduction is the proposed basis.

absolute: History of seizures (dose-related seizures may occur)
Moderate or severe renal impairment (CrCl <=50 mL/min)
relative: Mild renal impairment (CrCl 51-80 mL/min) - use with caution, seizure risk
Concurrent use of any other form of 4-aminopyridine (compounded aminopyridine) - additive seizure risk
Prior anaphylaxis or hypersensitivity reaction to the drug
monitor: Renal function (creatinine clearance) before and during therapy

preg: There are limited human data on use in pregnancy. Animal studies showed developmental toxicity at higher exposures. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit clearly justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether dalfampridine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Dalfampridine is eliminated almost entirely unchanged by the kidneys, so renal function critically determines plasma exposure. It is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment (CrCl <=50 mL/min), in whom the drug accumulates and substantially raises the risk of seizures. In mild renal impairment (CrCl 51-80 mL/min) plasma concentrations may approach those seen in patients taking higher (more seizure-prone) doses, so use with caution. Estimate creatinine clearance before starting and periodically during treatment; given the typical age range of MS patients, clinically meaningful renal impairment is plausible and should be actively assessed.
hepatic: Dalfampridine undergoes no relevant hepatic metabolism (it is excreted essentially unchanged by the kidneys), so no dose adjustment is anticipated for hepatic impairment.

major: Other forms of 4-aminopyridine, including compounded aminopyridine - do NOT use together; additive exposure markedly increases seizure risk
moderate: Cimetidine - inhibits the OCT2 transporter and increases dalfampridine plasma levels (dalfampridine is an OCT2 substrate)
Other organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2) inhibitors - may raise dalfampridine concentrations and seizure risk
Drugs that lower the seizure threshold - additive seizure risk
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food has no clinically meaningful effect on overall exposure
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacokinetic interaction established; alcohol does not change the requirement to avoid exceeding 10 mg twice daily
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference reported

serious: Anaphylaxis and other severe hypersensitivity reactions
rare: Severe allergic reactions involving respiratory or cardiovascular compromise
emergency: Anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, throat/tongue swelling, hives, hypotension)

monitoring: Renal function (creatinine clearance) before starting and periodically during therapy
Signs and symptoms of seizure activity
counsel: Swallow the tablet whole - do NOT crush, chew, split or dissolve it
Take one tablet about every 12 hours; never take more than two tablets in 24 hours
If you miss a dose, skip it - do NOT take an extra tablet or double up, as this raises the risk of seizures
Stop the drug and seek urgent help if you have a seizure, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as trouble breathing or swelling of the face/throat
Tell your doctor about kidney problems and any history of seizures before taking this medicine
pk: Improvement in walking seen during controlled trials within weeks of starting therapy
Peak plasma concentration approximately 3-4 hours after the extended-release tablet
Store at 25 C (77 F) with excursions permitted to 15-30 C; protect from light and moisture, keep in original container
pearls: Dose-related SEIZURES are the key safety concern - never exceed 10 mg twice daily; higher doses add no benefit and increase seizure risk
CONTRAINDICATED in patients with a history of seizures
CONTRAINDICATED in moderate or severe renal impairment (CrCl <=50 mL/min) because the renally eliminated drug accumulates and raises seizure risk
Check renal function (estimate CrCl) before starting and during treatment; in mild impairment (CrCl 51-80) exposure may approach higher-dose levels, so use caution
Avoid concurrent use of any other form of 4-aminopyridine / compounded aminopyridine - additive exposure and seizure risk
Counsel patients to swallow tablets whole and never to take an extra or doubled dose after a missed dose
Watch for anaphylaxis and for urinary tract infections, both reported with therapy
missed: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do NOT take a double dose or an extra tablet to make up for a missed one - taking more than the prescribed 10 mg twice daily increases the risk of seizures.
overdose: Overdose may cause seizures, confusion, tremor, sweating, agitation and other excitatory CNS effects. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, control seizures, and monitor closely. Because dalfampridine is renally eliminated, ensuring adequate renal clearance and supportive measures are central to management.
